source_backed_facts.fact: The chapel was constructed in 1925 by local craftsmen and is identified as Western Craftsman architecture.
The main chapel is a rectangular building measuring approximately 22 feet by 50 feet.
The walls are horizontally laid, bark-stripped lodgepole pine logs with saddle-notched corners and sawn log ends extending beyond the walls.
A moderately pitched wood-shake gable covers the main body and similar smaller gables cover documented projections.
Raking-edge fascias extend beyond the roof plane and terminate in tapered spear-like ends.
The front entrance is a beveled vertical-plank door with decorative surface-mounted wrought-iron latch and hinges.
Lattice casement windows occur along the nave and sacristy side walls; a large fixed-sash altar window is centered in the altar-end wall.
A roughly 14-foot-square sacristy flanks the sanctuary to the northeast.
The complex is described as oriented toward the southeast and enclosed by a lodgepole-pine buck-and-pole fence.
